answer: With a Wesolowski-style time-lock, each identity must compute sequential modular squarings, each step depending on the last; a GPU cannot divide one chain to reduce its elapsed time. Clones named harbor, jade, and nectar each require a separate run. Hardware may run chains concurrently, but cannot erase per-chain latency, so mass Sybil creation faces a physical time bottleneck. The succinct proof lets verifiers check the work efficiently.
